name: Battle_ActionUi_Update
summary: Per-frame state machine (states 0x102E..0x10E6) of the battle action UI object: advances member flags, queued messages and balloon spawns and returns 1 when the state finishes.
evidence: Two named callers, Battle_AutoAction_UpdateMembers and Ui_PartyMemberSlot_Update, tick this object, and the 44 named callees (Battle_ActionUi_RefreshMemberFlags, Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry, Battle_PlayBalloonSpawnSe, Battle_AddStateFlags) are all battle-UI helpers; the damaged registers affect register allocation only, not the role.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update2D
signature: int Battle_ActionUi_Update2D(BattleActionUi* self, u32 frame, u32 arg3, void* callback)
summary: Battle action-UI state machine for the sprite-based member visuals (states 0x1367/0x1399/0x13DA/0x149B), pushing party-widget updates and battle messages; it aborts when battle work +0x4244 is 0, i.e. it only runs inside a 3D battle.
evidence: Named caller Battle_ActionUi_UpdateMemberVisibility and the twin split by callee set (this one uses Battle_UpdatePartyWidgets/Ui_AutoCloseMessageWindow, 0x003F5528 uses Model_SetupPartsFromTable/Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend) support the 2D-member vs 3D-model split; the +0x4244 guard is only a 3D-battle gate, so the '2D' part refers to the sprite path inside a 3D battle and stays the weakest element.

name: Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableB
signature: void Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableB(FieldScene* scene, u8* records, u32 count)
summary: Spawns the field actors described by a placement-record table: resolves the model set per record and initialises gimmick/NPC actors with talk/emote balloons.
evidence: Its single named caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable, plus callees Field_ActorGimmick_InitFromRecord, Field_Npc_InitTalkBalloons, Field_Npc_InitEmoteBalloon and Field_GetActorModelSetIndex, show a per-record actor spawner; the 'B' only separates it from the 0x00336BE4/0x00337030 helpers.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update3D
signature: int Battle_ActionUi_Update3D(BattleActionUi* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, void* arg4)
summary: Battle action-UI state machine for the 3D member models (states 0x13DA/0x1399...): selects units, drives model part setup, camera focus blending and display-list builds.
evidence: Called from Battle_ActionUi_UpdateMemberVisibility and the split block 0x003F6262; callees Model_SetupPartsFromTable, Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend, Gfx_BuildDisplayList and Ui_PartyStatus_CacheCostume distinguish it from its 2D twin and confirm the 3D model path.

name: Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableThumb
signature: void Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableThumb(FieldScene* scene, u8* records, u32 count)
summary: Thumb build of the scene-table spawner: iterates the scene's placement array and creates the object, registers its NPC actions and resolves its anim set.
evidence: Its only caller is Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable and its callees (Field_RegisterNpcActions, Field_GetActorAnimSetIndex, Field_GetObjectHandleA, Party_ResolveAppearanceVariantIndex) match the ARM twin; the damaged unaff_r4/r5 do not change the role.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecordB
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecordB(FieldScene* scene, u32 record, int* extra)
summary: Record-driven scene-object setup that resolves the record's model set and jump location and inserts the object into the scene's tree map; the decompiled body is merged with neighbouring functions, so the exact record layout is not readable.
evidence: Named caller Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects and callees Field_SpawnObjectRecordA, Map_ResolveJumpLocationId and Container_TreeMap_InsertOrFindB still fit a record initialiser, but the 660-line body contains several merged functions (Ghidra bad-instruction warnings at 0x00340A02), so no single-role name is provable.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecord
summary: Creates a field scene object from a map/status record: spawns the object, copies the record's sub-structure into it and resolves its jump location id.
evidence: Callers Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects / maybe_Actor_LinkSubObjectNodes and the copied sub-record fields plus Map_ResolveJumpLocationId support the initialiser reading, but Ghidra lost every callee (list empty) and the tail is unrecovered, so the name stays provisional.

name: BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelsByState
signature: int BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelsByState(BattleScene* self, BattleMember* member, unsigned arg3, int index)
summary: State-dependent unit model update: scene state 0/4/5 delegates to BattleScene_BuildPartyModel, state 1 scans the four unit lists at battle+0x428C and adjusts the matching unit model.
evidence: The switch on self->f_f0 with explicit cases and the named callees BattleScene_BuildPartyModel, BattleScene_BuildMemberModel, BattleScene_AdjustUnitModelTransform and BattleScene_AdjustUnitNodeTransformB pin the role; there is still no caller, so only the update function itself is confirmed.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0
summary: Lays out the battle party models and then scans the four unit lists for model variants 3/4, writing the resulting visibility/colour descriptor and self->f_340; the 24-byte symbol may be a Ghidra split of the following 0x00609498 routine.
evidence: Only caller Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseHandles and callee BattleScene_LayoutPartyModels are known, and the body runs straight on into 0x00609498, so the entry-point boundary - not the effect - is what keeps this below 0.5.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateCompositeB
summary: Battle actor-action state machine on actor+0x623 (states 0x17E1..): hides/updates attach slots and animation frames, spawns model-actor popups and finishes from the +0x1385/+0x1386 bytes; the letter is only an ordinal in the CompositeA..D family.
evidence: Callees Model_Equip_ApplyCharacterEquipment, Model_AttachSlot_HideAll, Model_Attach_UpdateAnimationFrame, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors and Battle_ActionModel_AnyUnitMarkerPending confirm an equipment/animation action, but there is no caller, no vtable slot and nothing mapping 'B' to a concrete action.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update2DContinuation
summary: Decompiler-split continuation block of the 2D battle action-UI loop (camera blend, costume cache, attach-slot resource swap); it uses unaff_r4..r9 and has no address-taken reference, so it is not a real function entry.
evidence: No callers or pointer references and callees Battle_Ui_UpdateUnitAnimState, Battle_Ui_PlayResultSound and the split block 0x003F6530 show this is a fragment of 0x003F463C rather than an independent routine.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update3DContinuation
summary: Decompiler-split tail of the 3D battle action-UI update: closes the command menu, updates unit expressions and commits model node changes; unaff registers and no references make it a fragment, not an entry point.
evidence: No callers/address-taken references; callees Battle_Ui_CloseCommandMenu, Battle_Ui_UpdateUnitExpression and Model_Equip_CommitNodeChanges duplicate the 0x003F5528 tail, with BADSPACEBASE damage.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateCompositeC
summary: Battle actor-action state machine (states 0x16E7..) that backs up unit actions, builds an effect descriptor from unit ids, spawns the effect plus model-actor popups and waits for effect and animation before returning 1.
evidence: 23 named callees (Battle_BackupUnitActions, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll/InitResource, Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty) describe an effect-based action, but the single caller recorded (Gfx_Scene2D_InitViewport) is clearly a mis-attributed neighbour and no vtable slot identifies which action it is.

name: Battle_StartActionSequence
summary: Starts a battle action sequence: updates the model animation list and actor models, sets the sequence state word +0x4D to 0xB7B, picks a non-empty unit list with the battle RNG and stores the primary target at +0x51.
evidence: The body's initial-state test/assignment (state 0xB7B), the four-list walk over battle+0x428C and the RNG call on battle+0x4218 match a sequence start; no caller exists, so the 'start' reading rests on the body alone.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_ResetAndCommit
summary: Tears down the tactics ('sakusen') screen: clears the float parameters of the four battle unit lists, applies tactic flags, re-places the unit array and restores the saved actor transforms.
evidence: Called from Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel; callees Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam on +0x4270/+0x4254/+0x428C lists, Ui_SakusenWindow_ApplyTacticFlags, BattleScene_PlaceUnitArray and BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelTransforms match a commit/restore at screen close.

name: Field_Actor_CreateSceneObjects
summary: Creates a field actor's scene object from a 16x16 sprite descriptor (vtable 0x00726908), links it into the actor's object list and creates the actor's collision objects.
evidence: Callers Ui_Overlay_AddEntry / Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup create overlay actors, and callees Mem_AllocAligned_2, Field_CreateCollisionObject, Field_SceneObject_FreeModelAndTrail and Object_IsHandleAlive confirm the scene-object + collision construction.

name: Field_Actor_CreateItemModelEffect
summary: Builds the 0x240-byte item-model object shown on a field actor: when the held item id is in the 0xAA3..0xB3A band it resolves the ItemRecord and picks the matching model variant, otherwise it loads model record 0x2DE.
evidence: The previous 'state effect' wording was too vague: Item_LookupRecord on the held item id with the range test id-0xAA3 < 0x98 and Ui_ItemModel_Load(0x2DE) prove this is an item-model effect, and the caller Field_Actor_TickEffectState only decides when to refresh it.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeC
summary: Merged sprite-object spawn body: several near-identical blocks build a sprite descriptor, call one of 0x004CC190 / 0x0044E34C / 0x00471D54 and register the resulting mesh with the scene.
evidence: Only the 0-byte recovered pseudocode exists (no dossier, no callers) and it contains several spawn variants merged together, so the 'type C' ordinal cannot be tied to any record type; the sprite-descriptor + mesh registration shape is all that is verifiable.

name: Field_Action_WalkUpdate
summary: Three-phase walk action: phase 0 moves the actor along the stored direction until the travel budget is spent and snaps to ground, phase 1 waits ~20 ticks and plays SE 0x104, phase 2 continues along the stored offset.
evidence: State byte self+0x2C with three phases, plus Field_SpriteObject_CaptureOffset, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and Sound_PlaySeById(0x104), make the walk reading explicit; there is still no caller to say which actor runs it.

name: Battle_Ui_RowPanel_BuildRows
summary: Rebuilds the per-member rows of the battle status/message panel: composes each member's name-plus-value row, spawns the row popups and plays the row sound.
evidence: Its only caller is Battle_Ui_RowPanel_Update and the callees Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, Sound_PlaySeById and Model_SetupPartsFromTable match a row rebuild; no pane/row literal survives, so 'rows' stays the ceiling of the name.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionSequence
summary: Update half of the battle action-sequence state machine started by 0x00173CD0: rescans the four unit lists, re-rolls the acting unit with the battle RNG and drives the target/hit stages.
evidence: Same object layout and 0x428C/0x4218/0x4244 battle-work offsets as 0x00173CD0, plus callees Battle_BuildTargetSlots, Ui_BalloonPool_SetFlag and Math_IntToFloat; the adjacency (0x34 bytes) and identical prologue make the start/update pair, but no caller exists.

name: maybe_Ui_DragScroll_Update
summary: Three-state touch-drag handler: resolves the scene object under the pointer, accumulates pointer deltas into the window offsets and stops the drag when the pointer returns to its origin.
evidence: State byte drag+9 with cases 0/1/2 and the Ui_Overlay_HideElementClass / Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState / Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation callees fit a drag gesture, but the only caller is an unnamed event gimmick routine, so 'scroll' is not proven.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_CreateVisual
summary: Builds the billboard sprite visual for a marker-like object and copies the marker transform onto it; the caller and several callees belong to the smith (crafting) menu, so the field-marker reading is not certain.
evidence: Only caller Ui_SmithMenu_OpenDefaultPage and callees Text_InvokeControlHandler / Ui_Talk_LoadDialogueLayout do not fit a plain field marker, while Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation and sprite id 0x32F are consistent with a marker billboard: the family stays unresolved.

name: Ui_ObjectList_BuildEntries
signature: void Ui_ObjectList_BuildEntries(UiObjectList* self, const unsigned char* entries, const unsigned char* end)
summary: Rebuilds the gimmick's draw-object list: allocates one 0x220-byte object per 2-byte descriptor entry, lays them out in a 5-column grid and appends them to the object list.
evidence: Both callers (Field_Gimmick_RebuildRows, Field_Gimmick_SetupListFromConfig) and the callee pair Ui_ObjectList_Clear / Mem_AllocAligned_2 show a list rebuild; the draw-object record size and grid layout are read directly from the body.

name: Field_GadgetList_CreateEntry
signature: int Field_GadgetList_CreateEntry(GfxOwner* owner, unsigned int resId)
summary: Creates one gadget-list entry for a resource id: resolves the resource through the handle table, allocates a 0x3C-byte wrapper built by Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_Create, appends it to the owner's list and returns the entry's field 7 (or -0x40 on failure).
evidence: The old 'AcquireType1' wording hid the role: all four callers are Field_GadgetList_FindOrAddByHandle / FindOrAddBySlotId / AddByActorName and Event_GetOrAddActorSlot, which need one cached entry per actor/handle, and the only constructor callee is Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_Create.

name: Ui_IconList_UpdateState
signature: void Ui_IconList_UpdateState(IconListModel* iconList, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Refreshes an icon grid: compares a progress value read from the save work with the cached state and, when they differ, rebuilds the grid through Ui_IconList_RefreshIcons and clears the hidden panes.
evidence: Callees Ui_IconList_RefreshIcons, Ui_SubObjectHost_Ctor and Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes plus the work+0x24A98 progress reads via 0x0066B004/0x0066B2CC lock the icon-grid role; the progress/threshold wording is still an interpretation.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_CommitAndStorePositions
signature: void maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_CommitAndStorePositions(UiSakusenWindow* window, u32 panel, int** actor)
summary: Walks the battle party/unit lists while closing the tactics screen and stores or tears down actor transforms; the decompilation contains bad instruction data, so the commit/store split is not readable.
evidence: Caller Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel and callees Battle_ActionAnimTable_Build / 0x0047C954 fit the same teardown as 0x0047CA34, but halt_baddata and overlapping instructions (0x0047C7A8 region) prevent confirming what is stored versus released.

name: maybe_Actor_HandleSpecialEvent
signature: void maybe_Actor_HandleSpecialEvent(int* actor, int eventId, unsigned int eventData)
summary: Applies a character-model state and status values for an actor: resolves linked actor handles by id and dispatches model slot state, effects and party-status values.
evidence: The named caller is Battle_HpGaugeWindow_SetCharacter - not Field_GetActorAttachment - and the callees Ui_PartyStatus_ApplyValue, Model_SetSlotState, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Field_GetActorAttachment describe a status/HP-gauge model setup, so the 'special event' wording is likely misleading but no better single role is provable.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantC
summary: Per-state part update for a field gimmick: state 0x10 moves all parts along the negated direction and plays an SE, other states apply per-part random offsets; the letter is only an ordinal among five near-identical variants.
evidence: State switch on 8/0x10/0x2E with Field_Gimmick_GetRandomPartOffset, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and Sound_PlaySeById matches the sibling variants; no caller or string can tell which physical gimmick uses this variant.

name: maybe_Actor_QueryInteraction
signature: unsigned int maybe_Actor_QueryInteraction(int* actor, int recordId)
summary: Only active in 3D battle mode: resolves a data-manager row by id and, for the ids 0x13/0x110/0x6A/0x6B, calls the linked actor's virtual or spawns an effect block and closes a window slot.
evidence: The battle-work +0x4244 gate, Game_GetDataManager row lookup via 0x0063E05C and the id-specific branches calling Actor_SpawnEffectBlock / Ui_Window_CloseSlot are clear, but the ids are unexplained and there is no caller, so 'interaction' is still a guess.

name: Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute
signature: int Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute(GfxModelPart* modelPart, int ownerHandle, unsigned int* attributeMask)
summary: Iterates the part's attribute records and, for each record whose mask intersects attributeMask, resolves the node handle and registers it with the owner via Ui_RegisterActor.
evidence: Eight callers now exist (Ui_Overlay_UpdateMarkerTrail, Ui_Overlay_ApplyMarkerAnimation, Ui_OverlaySlot_TryInteract, Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute) and all pass a mask plus owner handle; the single callee Ui_RegisterActor is the registration step, confirming a part-attribute application pass.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_UpdateVisual
summary: Switches on the marker record's type byte to play the matching SE and build the matching marker sprite, then attaches the gadget and refreshes the marker's UI state.
evidence: The switch on record byte +1 with Sound_PlaySeById(0xEE7) / Sound_CommandQueue_Push_2 and three un-named marker builders is real, but the same body also calls Craft_BuildIngredientOwnershipList and Ui_SmithMenu_PushCommandPage (smith menu), and the three builders are still unnamed, so 'marker' is not proven.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantE
summary: Part-update variant: state 8 moves all parts of the owner actor group by the negated basis vector, otherwise it updates the attachments and part records and plays the SE.
evidence: Only the helper pair and record global differ from the other four variants (Field_Actor_UpdateAttachment, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, Sound_PlaySeById); the ordinal letter is unavoidable because nothing references this slot by name.

name: Field_Actor_SpawnAttachedEffect
summary: Builds a sprite/effect descriptor and creates the actor's attached 2D effect through the scene sprite system once the actor handle resolves, binding the effect by name.
evidence: Callees Mem_AllocAligned_2, Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName and the handle-table lookup on the actor's effect timer show descriptor + attached effect creation; there is no caller and the descriptor constants are the only naming evidence.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantA
summary: Resolves the referenced actor, walks its parts and places each with the variant-A helpers while playing the SE.
evidence: Same skeleton as the four sibling variants (handle lookup, 0x004A1E00, 0x00650D34 loop) with different helper addresses; no caller or string disambiguates the ordinal.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantB
summary: Same part-walk as variant A using the variant-B helper pair; it resolves the owner actor's parts, places them and plays the SE.
evidence: Structurally identical to 0x005DDA54 with only the helper addresses changing (Sound_PlaySeById, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, 0x004A1DEC); the earlier 'tint' claim is unsupported and has been dropped.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartsVariantD
summary: Same part-walk skeleton as variants A/B/E with the variant-D helper pair and record global.
evidence: Only the helper addresses and the record global differ from the other variants; there is no caller, so the name is the family role plus an ordinal.

name: maybe_Ui_ActorAttachSlot_SetHandle
signature: void maybe_Ui_ActorAttachSlot_SetHandle(u8* slot, u8 value, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Writes a state value into a slot, resolves the unit's actor handles and registers the matching one into a per-command attachment slot (unit+0x4A88/+0x4B34/+0x4B7C/+0x4BCC) through Ui_RegisterActor.
evidence: The 14 callers are action/effect end paths (Field_Action_WalkEnd, ActorAction_EndMove, Gfx_Effect2D_EndFrame, Actor_Action_Trail_End, Ui_SceneWindow_Close), and the body ends in Ui_RegisterActor(unit+0x4A88/0x4Bxx, resolvedHandle, 0) - a shared attach-slot registration helper, not an overlay marker routine; 'marker state' was wrong, but the exact slot semantics are still damaged.

name: Ui_ModelPreview_UpdateSpin
summary: Advances the preview pane's spin angle from its lazily created rotation state, applies it with Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation and attaches or releases the accessory mesh.
evidence: The body is a shortened copy of the named Ui_ListRow_UpdateWeaponPreview (0x462F7C): same 0x1D4-byte lazy state object, same Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation and Model_Attach/ReleaseAccessoryMesh calls; only the caller is missing.

name: Actor_ApplyModelPartsB
summary: When the actor has part data, asks ActorPart_GetPartIds for the ids selected by the UI mode byte (work+8->+0x48, +0x281), binds the matching animation and creates the sprite mesh.
evidence: Caller Party_Status_SelectPage and callees ActorPart_GetPartIds, Anim_BindWithDefaultContext, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh confirm a part application pass driven by the UI overlay mode byte; the B suffix separates it from 0x0022D110.

name: Model_ResolveHandleAndRefresh
summary: Refresh pass after a model change: refreshes the cached sprite size and cell visibility, re-applies the shared default animation clip and stores the resolved model-slot handle in f_244.
evidence: The two callees Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate and Field_SceneObject_RefreshModelAndCellVisibility are now named and the body only reads/writes model fields; with no callers left, the exact trigger for the refresh is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenFromByte
summary: Releases the window's 0x5A4 sub-object, bumps a global open counter and opens the data panel whose type comes from a global byte; the live callee list no longer contains Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple, so the panel role is unconfirmed.
evidence: Its only caller is maybe_Field_Marker_UpdateVisual (a smith/marker path) and the live callees are Ui_SubObjectHost_Ctor, Party_EntryMatchesSelectedId and Game_GetWork - not the data-panel helper the old evidence cited - so the honest verdict is 'unverified opener'.

name: Field_Actor_TriggerNearbySameType
summary: Triggers the situation reaction of every other actor of the same sub-type within the global radius, plays SE 0xEE and plays this actor's own situation effect if anything reacted.
evidence: Caller Field_Actor_UpdatePush plus callees Sound_PlaySeById(0xEE) and Field_Actor_PlaySituationEffect(0x003DD2D0) confirm the proximity check and the reaction dispatch; the damaged registers only affect the radius constant.

name: Ui_Window_InitSlotB
summary: Builds the window's third text/portrait slot once (guarded by f_26D): scans the type-3 text table for the window character f_273, allocates the 0x23C message widget, inserts it and copies the window position.
evidence: Caller Ui_Status_PlayAilmentPose; Game_GetDataManager + the 0x0063F4F4 table scan and Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x23C) show a message-widget slot built for a character record, so the 'B' slot role is confirmed even though the widget's exact use is not.

name: Model_Actor_UpdateAttachmentAndSync
summary: Per-frame attachment sync: updates the weapon model, then either blends the actor position toward the attachment anchor or refreshes the attachment from the character record.
evidence: Callees Model_Actor_UpdateAttachment, maybe_Model_Actor_OnAttachmentChanged (0x00377BD0) and Model_SetupPartsFromTable match the two-branch sync; there is no caller, so the branch trigger is unknown.

name: Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActorsB
summary: Second linking pass: matches battle party/unit list entries to their UI widgets by actor handle and invokes the widget's bind slot +0x98.
evidence: Six callers now include Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateLinkState, Battle_Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchors/MoveToAnchor and Text_Window_UpdateShowFlags, and the callees Battle_IsUnitKindShownInMemberUi + Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ show list-to-widget matching.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionB
summary: State-driven reaction on a field gimmick: state 8 plays SE 0xE4E, state 0x10 sets the effect direction and plays the SE, state 0x28 resolves the attached gadget and applies a part action.
evidence: Mirrors the reaction-A routine 0x005D9334 with only the state ids and helper calls changing (Sound_PlaySeById, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, Field_ActorActionSet_Init); no caller, so the reaction type rests on the state ids.

name: Ui_ItemModel_CreateAttached
signature: void Ui_ItemModel_CreateAttached(UiListWidget* list, int delta, u32 arg3, int* listHandle)
summary: Allocates a 0x240-byte item-model object and attaches it to the list widget so the row can show an item model.
evidence: The single caller is now named Ui_Window_ApplyItemModelEvent, which handles item-model events for a window, and the 0x240 allocation matches the item-model object size used by Ui_ItemModel_Load; the body itself is still damaged (coprocessor_*).

name: Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget
signature: u32 Ui_Overlay_ApplyShapeToTarget(FieldObject* object, u32 arg2, u32 geometry, u32 mask)
summary: Resolves the overlay target under the cursor and applies the matching entry's model-part attribute or object hook; used by the marker-trail update.
evidence: Caller Ui_Overlay_UpdateMarkerTrail and callees Ui_Overlay_FindTargetUnderCursor, Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute, Field_Object_UpdateHook and Ui_Overlay_CheckEntryPlacement now name every step, so the shape/mask application reading holds.

name: maybe_Field_CreateActorRuntimeState
summary: Builds a large stack descriptor (billboard vtable, floats, sprite flags) and creates a sprite-mesh object with an animation clip from it; the presence of Item_MatchesEquipCategory suggests an item/prop preview actor rather than a plain field actor.
evidence: No callers; callees mix Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh and Anim_Clip_Start (sprite actor creation) with Item_MatchesEquipCategory, and the descriptor is partly stack garbage, so 'runtime state' is not a verified role.

name: Gfx_Actor_ApplyAppearanceB
summary: Post-model-change appearance path: validates the model handle and scene mode, resolves the model set index and restarts the animation clip set.
evidence: Callees Field_GetActorModelSetIndex, Field_GetActorAnimSpeedMultiplier and Anim_ClipSet_Build are all named and fit the appearance re-application; the B suffix separates it from 0x0031B114 and no caller exists.

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_SpawnEffectSprite
summary: Resolves an actor from a handle, builds a world position from the actor origin plus the probe offsets and draws a sprite through the scene sprite context.
evidence: Callers are collision-style code (Field_Actor_CheckWallCollision, maybe_Actor_UpdateFollowTargetMotion) and callees Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteEx / Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext only prove 'draw a sprite at a probe point'; whether it is an effect sprite or a debug contact marker is unresolved.

name: Field_CreateSpriteActor
summary: Builds a 2D sprite descriptor, allocates and constructs a field actor through the shared factory, registers it, places it at the scene camera position and replaces the previous handle.
evidence: Callees Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh, Field_SceneObject_ClearPartFlag, Actor2D_ReRegisterObject and the sprite-actor vtable 0x00726418 confirm the construction; there is no caller to pin which subsystem requests the actor.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushBalloonMessages
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_PushBalloonMessages(BattleUiContext* context, u32 recordHandle, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Short Thumb fragment that de-duplicates a message id against a stack list and pushes a battle message entry; unaff registers and a 60-byte boundary make it a split block rather than a readable routine.
evidence: No caller; callees Battle_CalcEffectivePower and Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ plus unaff_r5/unaff_r6/in_stack registers show the decompilation is damaged and the 'balloon messages' wording is only a guess from the battle-UI neighbourhood.

name: Actor_Action_InitState
summary: Initialises an actor action: detects the special state byte 'x', stores the action-state flag/timer and plays the action's start sound when not in that state.
evidence: Vtable-only entry, but the prologue (Sound_GetPlayer, Sound_CommandQueue_Push_2, Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle) plus the state flag/timer stores match an action initialiser; no caller names the concrete action family.

name: Item_ApplySpecialModelParams
summary: For a small set of item ids it resolves the item record's display actor at +0x110 and pushes shared layout row parameters through pane virtuals +0xA4/+0xA0; otherwise it re-triggers the actor when the field-preview flag is set.
evidence: Game_GetDataManager, Game_GetWork, Actor_SelectAnimEntry0 and Item_IsRecipeCraftable as callees fit the item display path, and the id list plus pane virtual calls are read directly; the exact id set is still implicit.

name: maybe_Actor_ApplyModelPartsA
summary: Applies a sprite/model descriptor to the actor: copies the descriptor, creates the sprite mesh, initialises the sprite object and registers the sub-object; the earlier ActorPart_GetPartIds reading is no longer supported by the live callees.
evidence: The live callees are std_memcpy, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh, Gfx_SpriteObject_InitFromDesc and Field_SceneObject_SetSubObjectC0 - not ActorPart_GetPartIds/Anim_BindWithDefaultContext as the old evidence claimed - and the Thumb body is damaged (unaff_r4/unaff_r6), so the 'model parts' name is doubtful.

name: Model_UpdateNamedNodeAndId
summary: When the global switch at 0x7A3168 is on it resets the model's 'N_ALL' node to the default transform and re-registers the model's two record ids; a second switch re-applies the render object at f_30C.
evidence: The 'N_ALL' literal, Model_GetNodeIdByName, Model_HasCommandByName and Model_CopyAnimParams are now all named and match the node/record re-registration; whether the switches make this a debug aid or a mandatory refresh is still runtime-dependent.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_SyncSlotFromHandle
summary: When no display slot is active it resolves the object behind the slot's handle and, if it is an overlay element of the expected class, calls its detach virtual (+0x3C with 4) and copies its slot id back into the slot object.
evidence: Its only caller is Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClassB and the listed callee Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord does not fit a slot sync, so the handle/class resolution is clear but the owner class and the slot/display meaning remain inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_SyncToActor
summary: Two-event handler: event 6 clears task+0x2AD; event 4 resolves the camera object, destroys pending objects, sets the flag, copies and optionally moves the position, picks the anchor point and re-resolves the object.
evidence: Caller Field_Object_InitSpriteFromParams and callees Gfx_Actor_BuildTransformFromPosition, Ui_DestroyObjectsOfClass and Ui_Overlay_ApplyPlacement fit a placement sync, but the 'sync to actor' target is still an interpretation of the copied position/anchor fields.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_UpdateOwner
summary: Refreshes a field object's sprite after its owner moves: takes the scene-mode byte, optionally re-registers the draw entry, then walks the returned ids 4 and 5 and calls the actor's sprite update.
evidence: Its only named relation is Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent (0x251230) and Save_SetNameBuffer_Tail, which do not pin an owner-change path; the id walk (4/5) and the scene-mode copy are unexplained.

name: Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActors
summary: Walks the battle party list at +0x4260 and binds each live actor to its member HUD widget through the tagged handle table and widget vtable +0x98.
evidence: Callers Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateLinkState, Text_Window_UpdateShowFlags and Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_LinkActors all need the actor/widget pairing, and the new callee Monster_LookupByActorId confirms it maps actor ids to monsters; the walk of f_4260 is read directly.

name: Ui_ListWidgetScreen_DispatchToChild
summary: Resolves the screen's child from the generation handle at +0x26C and dispatches by child class: the list class gets Anim_SaveStateToSlot plus a bag-work update, the second class its own +0xE1 callback, the third the field-object wakeup callback.
evidence: Caller Ui_ListWidgetScreen_UpdateState; the handle resolution (0x1FFFFF index + generation check on 0x007B80C0) and three class-tag walks are structural, and Anim_SaveStateToSlot / Text_ExecuteCommand are now named callees, so only the dispatch meaning remains inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_ArcListWindow_AssignEntrySlot
summary: Scans up to 26 entry slots for the entry selected by the work index byte at +0x5691, compares it with the active list at work+0x5628 and attaches the surviving entry through its vtable +0x98.
evidence: Caller Ui_ArcListWindow_SetupFromPlayerActor and the split block 0x0049D806 fit a slot assignment, but the body is heavily damaged (coprocessor_function2, unaff_r5, in_cr0/in_s1) and the selected-entry logic cannot be read, so the name stays below 0.5.

name: Battle_Ui_ResolvePopupTarget
summary: Resolves the target for animation record 0x10E: walks the battle actor list, matches the record handle, notifies the matching actor and returns 0xFFFFFFFF when nothing matches.
evidence: Caller Battle_Ui_UpdateLevelUpPopup and callees Data_LookupSubRecord, Actor_ResolveReferenceObject and Field_SceneObject_ShowAndSelectEntry show the record-to-actor resolution; the popup linkage itself is still the inference.

name: maybe_Gfx_Model_UpdateLodByScreenSizeB
summary: Second distance/size LOD selector: resolves the model through the self->f_28->f_238 handle and its 0x44 object id and applies the same decision as 0x004E2020.
evidence: Callers Field_Object_ApplyPlacementAnim and maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateStateAnimation fit a per-frame LOD update, but the recorded callees Battle_Effect_SpawnFocusPoint/B do not look like LOD code, so either the callee list or the LOD reading is contaminated by neighbouring symbols.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdatePartEffectParams
summary: Walks the gimmick's 0xC-stride part slots, matches partId, resolves the attached actor/effect object through the handle map and updates its parameters with a random variation.
evidence: The slot loop with the partId compare and the gadget-handle-map lookup is read directly, and the callees (Field_Actor_CreateAttachedEffectParts, Ui_AreAllSpanGroupsIdle, std_FastSinCos, Math helpers) support parameter updates; no caller names the effect kind.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionA
summary: State-driven gimmick reaction: state 8 plays SE 0xE4E, state 0x10 sets the effect direction and plays the SE, state 0x16 applies the follow-up part action.
evidence: Case values 8/0x10/0x16 with Sound_PlaySeById, Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and Field_ActorActionSet_Init are explicit; the A suffix is confirmed only as the counterpart of reaction B (0x005D94B8).

name: maybe_Ui_QuestIcon_CreateC
signature: int maybe_Ui_QuestIcon_CreateC(UiIconHost* host, IconRecord* out, unsigned int handle)
summary: Resolves an NPC of class 0x007C4D4C from the handle, looks up its entry by sub-state (f_94) or id (+0x36) and builds the icon record.
evidence: The class check and the two lookups are read directly, but the callees (Party_GetMemberIdAtCurrentPage, Spirit_CountRosterEntries, Field_SceneTransition_IsBusy) do not single out a quest icon and no layout string is present, so the icon family and the 'C' ordinal remain guesses.

name: maybe_BattleScene_CreateFormationWidgets
summary: Creates one widget per entry of the battle work's +0x4E90 list using the shared UI singleton and render context; the list's meaning (formation/enemy panel) is not labelled anywhere.
evidence: No caller; the loop over f_4E90/f_4E94/f_4E98 with Engine_ResourceNode_CtorBase and Gfx_GetRenderContext shows widget creation, but nothing identifies the list as a formation table.

name: maybe_BattleUi_UpdateMemberSlotTransforms
summary: Rebuilds the transform of each four-list unit's body-400 model from its rotation/position and resets the battle time tracks.
evidence: The four 0x1C-stride lists at battle+0x428C, Model_SetupPartsFromTable and BattleScene_ResetTimeTracks are read directly, but the single caller (0x005ADC54, labelled a message-window scroll update) leaves the UI role unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateMemberPath
summary: Per-frame update that walks the gimmick's actor slot array, moves/aims live actors through the effect helpers and recomputes the active state ids.
evidence: The handle-table arithmetic plus Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and Math_TransformOffsetPoint are clear, but nothing identifies a 'member path' and there is no caller; the slot array could be any part/actor list.

name: Field_Gimmick_ApplyEffectConfig
summary: Applies the current gimmick configuration to its effect parts: resolves the target actor, computes a unit direction and distance, pushes it into the effect object and copies the config words selected by the variant byte.
evidence: Callees Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, std_FastSinCos, Battle_Ui_TargetGroup_CalcBounds and Field_Actor_TickEffectState fit direction/distance application; the meaning of the copied words is still inferred, and no caller exists.

name: Field_Object_ReleaseSpriteResourceB
summary: Second sprite/model release path: validates the packed handle at self+0x370, calls manager vtable+0x3C with category 4 and applies the manager byte at +0x88 through Field_SpawnObject_ApplyRecord.
evidence: Its only caller is Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClassB and the body repeats the confirmed release sequence of the sibling on a second handle field; which sprite class maps to category 4 is still unknown.

name: Actor_FindComponentInState
summary: Walks the 32 component slots of an actor and returns the object behind the handle of the first component whose state query (0x00639954) reports stateId.
evidence: 0x00639954 is a proven active-state test (unit, stateId), and its caller maybe_Actor_HasSpecialModelPart only needs 'does any component have this state, and which object is it' - the old 'event' wording came from an unnamed assumption.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateMemberBalloons
summary: Updates one battle member's balloon row: takes the id pair from the object's vtable (+0x48/+0x60), resolves it through 0x00632760, compares against the actor lists and stores the mode byte at self+0x494.
evidence: The vtable id pair, 0x00632760 lookup and four-list scan are confirmed, but its only caller (0x004378DC, CompositeD) and the callees Ui_Shop_GetItemAttributeB / Container_GetPooledEntryThunk do not mention balloons, so the balloon wording is unsupported.

name: Actor_CreateModelPart
signature: void Actor_CreateModelPart(Actor* actor, u32 partId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates one model part from a part descriptor: fills the part object at actor->f_BC, calls the optional builder with the actor transform, swaps the new part into actor->f_210 and releases the old handle.
evidence: Caller Actor_CreateActionTable and the descriptor fill plus f_210 swap are read directly; the remaining callees are partly generic (Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy, Ui_SlotMachine_DtorBase) but the part creation is local to this body.

name: ModelPreview_ResetToDefaultRecord
summary: Resets a preview/model slot: stops any sub-animation on the handle at self+0x30C (vtable +0x40 with 4) and re-applies character record 0 through Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord.
evidence: Caller Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClass and the single callee Actor_ApplyNameStringsFromRecord(self, 0) prove the reset-to-record-0 path; 'ModelPreview' is inherited from the slot's neighbours rather than proven.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_AssignEntryOrder
summary: Re-numbers overlay-like entries: walks the 0xC-byte entries from index 1, writes a running counter into word +0x8A and calls 0x003E7110(element, index); the anchor entry gets order 0.
evidence: No caller, damaged registers (unaff_r4, overlapping instructions at 0x00239EFC) and callees Field_Actor_ResolveHandle / Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteMeshPartCommands that do not fit an ordering pass; only the entry stride and counter store are legible.

name: Ui_MonsterBookEntry_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a monster-book list entry: installs g_uiMonsterBookEntryVtable at self, builds the 0x98-byte child resource node and stores it into the entry's child pointer.
evidence: Decisive: the first store is `*self = &g_uiMonsterBookEntryVtable`, and the body then allocates and constructs the entry's 0x98-byte resource node - a constructor of the monster-book entry class, confirmed by the vtable symbol.

name: Actor_RequestLinkedModelStates
summary: Walks the actor's linked sub-object chain and requests model state 2/3 for each loaded sub-object whose state byte is unset; called from the status-window scene rebuild.
evidence: Caller Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects and the state request via 0x003368C8 while following the link list are read directly; the class-hash lookups and Party_FindEntryById only resolve the owning entry.

name: Ui_Smith_FindStandObject
summary: Resolves the smith-menu stand object: follows self+0x1C->f_3C through the type hash table and walks the vtable chain until it matches g_smithStandActor3DClass.
evidence: Both callers are smith-menu routines (Ui_Smith_StartSequence, Ui_Smith_UpdateHitEffect) and the comparison is against the literal g_smithStandActor3DClass, so the generic 'window sub-object' wording was under-specific.

name: Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyLabels
summary: Loops up to five party slots, resolves each unit actor (slot 4 special-cased), finds the label object via the class hash table and sets it from the per-slot 6-byte label record.
evidence: Callees Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple, Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ and PartyGroup_GetSlotActor, plus the five-slot loop writing 6-byte records at self+0x1404, confirm the label update; there is no caller.

name: maybe_Field_MultiPart_AttachActors
summary: Resolves the part's scene target and two actor handles through the handle table and registers the pair with the scene via Ui_RegisterActor.
evidence: No caller; callees Ui_RegisterActor, Field_SceneObject_ReleaseHandleAndEffects and Ui_StatusWindow_RemoveSlotObjects make the two-handle attachment clear, but the owning class ('multi part') is inferred from the field-object neighbourhood.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_ApplyTacticFlagsB
signature: void maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_ApplyTacticFlagsB(UiSakusenWindow* window, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32** arg4)
summary: Thumb duplicate of 0x0047C46C: the same tactic-panel type dispatch and slot-member application, with lost unaff_r4/r7 registers preventing a clean signature.
evidence: Caller 0x0047C7A8 and callees Menu_SetSelectedActorId, Ui_GetCore, 0x0063FD24 action rows show the tactics-screen member application; the duplicate marker 'B' is all the suffix means.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionModel_SetNodeStateA
signature: void maybe_Battle_ActionModel_SetNodeStateA(int* actionModel, int startFrame, int endFrame)
summary: Applies an animation/node state to a battle action model: resets the node list, sets frame and end frame (falling back to the animation length), releases the model handle and re-applies the visibility mode at +0xF22.
evidence: The node/frame stores and the callees Battle_ReleaseSceneDisplay, Model_Actor_UpdateArmAttachmentAnim and Field_SceneObject_ShowAndSelectEntry fit a node-state setter, but the owner class is not established and A/B are ordinals.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionModel_SetNodeStateB
summary: Twin of 0x00484EBC: resets the node list, releases the model handle at self[0x44] and re-applies the visibility mode at +0xF22, branching on the battle 3D/2D mode.
evidence: Vtable slot 7 with no callers; the body is 0x00484EBC minus the frame arguments and branches on battle+0x4244, so the family role is likely but the class and the A/B split are not verifiable.

name: maybe_Ui_HandleArray_CreateNode
summary: Allocates a 0x220-byte node for a layout part id, registers it in the handle table and binds the UI layout listeners.
evidence: Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x220) and Ui_HandleArray_ReleaseAll are named, but the other callees (Field_SceneObject_CopyRecord, Ui_SkillPointWindow_DeletingDtor) are generic, and no caller exists to say whether the node is a UI layout part or a scene record.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_LinkActors
summary: Sub-update of the member screen that binds each member slot to its field actor/model and target markers, then syncs the per-member model transforms.
evidence: Its only caller is Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_Update and it calls Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActors (0x003C4D9C) plus Model_CreateAttachedEffect / Gfx_Node_FaceObject, matching a per-member binding pass; the target-marker half is inferred.

name: maybe_BattleUi_ArrangeMemberSlots
summary: Places the battle party member models at their formation-table coordinates and triggers each slot's vtable +0x98.
evidence: Model_SetupPartsFromTable and the formation-coordinate copies are read directly, but the only caller is 0x005ADC54 (labelled a message-window scroll update), so the 'member slot arrangement' owner is not confirmed.

name: Battle_SetUnitListsVisible
summary: Sets the float parameter to 1 on all four battle unit lists (+0x428C stride 0x1C) and calls each list's unit vtable +0x98.
evidence: Its twin 0x005AD704 does the identical loop with 0, so the pair is a show/hide toggle; the loop over the four +0x428C lists and Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam are read directly, though no caller gives the screen.

name: Battle_SetUnitListsHidden
summary: Same as Battle_SetUnitListsVisible with visibility 0 on all four battle unit lists.
evidence: Identical body to 0x005AD5BC with Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam(list, 0); the visible/hidden pair is established by the two adjacent bodies.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseSlotB
signature: void Ui_Window_ReleaseSlotB(UiWindow* uiWindow, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Second-half release sequence applied to the handle at self+0x1C6: validates the handle, calls vtable+0x40(obj, 4), releases it through 0x001C7570(world+0x54, handle) and calls self vtable+0x3C(self, 4).
evidence: Same release sequence as the confirmed 0x00378148 on a second handle field, and Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy is a named callee; the only caller (0x001CC6D8) is itself a low-confidence function, so the 'B' remains a duplicate marker.

name: maybe_BattleScene_HideDistantUnits
summary: Releases actor handles of battle units that fail a distance check and are not referenced by three battle-work lookups.
evidence: No caller; the float threshold comes from a register Ghidra lost, and the callees (Party_FindMemberOrdinalInSlot, Party_CountActive, Ui_Shop_GetItemAttributeB) are shared lookups, so 'hide distant' is only the shape of the body.

name: maybe_Sound_PlayActorSe
summary: Resolves an event actor slot index to its actor and forwards the 3-byte {seId, 0xFF, modelByte} struct to 0x005F7F78, taking the third byte from the actor model at +0x534.
evidence: The slot walk uses the documented event state f_430/f_434 (0x10 stride) and the callee recorded is now CSCameraEnd (0x00147C70, a misnamed neighbour), while 0x005F7F78 remains unidentified - so 'plays an SE' is still an inference from the struct bytes.

name: maybe_Sound_PlayActorSeEx
signature: void maybe_Sound_PlayActorSeEx(int actorIndex, u8 seId, u8 volume)
summary: Same event-actor-slot resolution as 0x00147BB4 but forwards an explicit third byte {seId, 0xFF, arg3} to 0x005F7F78.
evidence: Identical slot-walk and 0x005F7F78 call shape as 0x00147BB4 with the third struct byte supplied by the caller; neither 0x005F7F78's semantics nor any caller confirms the sound reading.

name: maybe_Event_ActorSlot_PlaySeEx
signature: void maybe_Event_ActorSlot_PlaySeEx(int actorIndex, u8 first, u8 b, u8 c)
summary: Same event-actor-slot resolution as 0x0014B878 but forwards the three caller bytes {first, c, b} to 0x005F7F78; a parameter post for an event actor.
evidence: The slot/handle validation idiom is identical to the 0x0014B878 family, but the callee is again the unidentified 0x005F7F78 and there are no callers, so the 'sound effect' part stays tentative.

name: maybe_Battle_Party_IsAnyMemberActorBusyEx
summary: Variant of 0x0016A2C8 that additionally skips members whose status query (vtable +0xE8 with 0x9A) is set, then applies the same actor-busy checks over the party list.
evidence: Same battle-work/party-list structure as 0x0016A2C8 plus the extra 0x9A status filter; no callers exist to say which battle phase needs the filtered variant, and the callees are shared helpers.

name: maybe_HandleTable_ReleaseAllLiveEntries
summary: Iterates the tracked-handle table (count at +0x18, handles at +0x8 stride 8) and for each entry still live in the global registry calls Field_Actor_PlayTalkMotionFromTable(obj, 3) and marks the slot released (+0xC = 1).
evidence: The registry/generation check and the per-slot released flag are clear, but the action value 3 passed to the now-named Field_Actor_PlayTalkMotionFromTable looks like a talk-motion state rather than a release, so the name overstates what is proven.

name: maybe_Anim_ApplyTrackPoseThumb
summary: Damaged Thumb decompilation of an animation-track pose application routine; unaff registers and fake arguments prevent a reliable reading, but the 0x60-stride track walk resembles 0x00267FF0.
evidence: Body full of unaff_rN/in_ZR/arg5..arg7 with a mis-detected function boundary; only Effect_HandleRelease and Os_GetGameWork are named, so the track-pose reading is structural only.

name: maybe_Anim_ApplyTrackPose
summary: Walks up to two track ids from self->f_CC, resolves each 0x60-byte animation record through self->f_1C and writes its position into the target object, then applies the transform and sets the needs-update byte.
evidence: The 0x60-stride record reads (f_10/f_20/f_30) and handle-table validation are read directly, but the only caller (0x00268418) is itself unnamed and the animation table is reached through hash constants, so 'track pose' is structural.

name: maybe_Anim_ApplyActionToMatchingHandles
signature: void maybe_Anim_ApplyActionToMatchingHandles(UiAnimOwner* animOwner, int startIndex, int endIndex)
summary: Scans the 0x40-byte handle entries at self+0x160 in [start,end), then walks the two field object lists (filter 4) to find the live object matching f_154/f_158 and its state bytes, reconciling the entries against its handle.
evidence: The handle-range scan and 0x40-stride slot array plus the object match on f_154/f_158 and +0x25A/+0x26A are read directly; there are no callers and the callees (Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy, Field_UpdateDrawList) are generic.

name: maybe_Ui_Actor_CalcOverlayPosition
summary: Resolves the object behind the UI context handle (work+0x48, +0x3B4) through the class hash table and derives an anchor from that object's f_A8/+0x78/+0x7C/f_A9/f_AA fields before the anchor math.
evidence: The handle resolution and field reads are clear, but the callee list mixes Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState, Model_CopyRootMatrix, Gfx_Trail_BuildPath and Field_Actor_ComputeCellTransitionOffset, and the outcome of the function is only partly legible.

name: Field_Actor_StopCurrentAction
summary: Resolves the actor's current action through the handle table and cancels it: calls the action's virtual +0x74 with (0,0) and then +0x3C with 4 to finish the state.
evidence: Caller Field_Action_SetRunState and the two explicit virtual calls make the cancellation clear; the numeric argument 4 and the action class are still inferred, and the callee list is empty because they are indirect calls.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_SetEntryFlag
signature: void maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_SetEntryFlag(UmaPanel* panel, u32 handle, u8 flag)
summary: Stores the flag in the horse-race panel's entry field self->f_798 and, when the handle passes the global handle-table check, notifies the panel's model object through virtual +0x7C.
evidence: The only reference is the constructor Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor passing its second and third arguments straight through; no named caller or callee confirms that f_798 is an entry flag, so the horse-race/entry wording stays inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_Component_FindAndNotify
summary: Finds the object of class g_uiComponentClass behind the handle at work+8->+0x48 +0x20 and calls its vtable +0xBC.
evidence: No callers and a single named callee (Os_GetGameWork); only the class-hash walk against g_uiComponentClass and the vtable+0xBC call are legible, so both the owner and the notification meaning remain guesses.

name: maybe_Model_IsInstanceRegistered
summary: Lazily builds a shared object when a guard byte is set, then resolves the object at obj[2]+0x6C via Field_FindObjectByMode(...,3) and returns 1 only if the returned handle's generation tag matches the global handle table.
evidence: Caller Ui_CampSelectWindow_Setup and callees Field_FindObjectByMode / Ui_ReleaseOwnedObjects are named, but the singleton it builds and the meaning of 'registered' are not identified, so the boolean test is the only solid part.

name: maybe_Actor_PlayEventSe
summary: Validates the handle at self+0x110 against the field object registry and posts a sound effect on it: codes 2/3 map to SE 0x1B (skipped when 0x00669250 reports 0x1C), 0x90 to 0x1C, 8/9 to 0x28.
evidence: Handle decode with the 0x001FFFFF/generation check followed by func_005E7848(handle, seId, 1) and the distinct SE ids per event code are read directly; no caller confirms the event-code mapping.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_BindActorHandle
signature: void maybe_Ui_Balloon_BindActorHandle(UiBalloon* self, u8 slot, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32* handle)
summary: If the passed handle resolves in the field object registry it stores the slot index at self+0x839 and sets self+0x838 = 1, then tail-calls 0x00100B74 with arg3.
evidence: Decisive correction: 0x00100B74 is wcslen, not an assert/trampoline, and the 'caller' Sound_PlayMenuSeByMode does not fit a balloon bind - so this is more likely a name/string helper than an actor-handle binder, and the body never stores the handle.

name: maybe_Ui_FaceIcon_SetOnOff
summary: When the cached +0x18 state differs it resolves the render handle, walks the node list and calls vtable +0x70 with the literal node name '...g3085b_off' or '...g3085b_off_on', then caches the new state.
evidence: The two node-name literals and the cached isOn flag prove an on/off node switch, and its callers (icon-list update, jackpot screen) are shared icon code - but nothing ties it specifically to face icons.

name: Field_Object_UpdateIfActor
summary: If the object has an attached actor (+0xF24) it resolves the handle, walks the class chain, and when the object derives from g_actorBaseClass calls 0x00669E24 and then 0x00669DD4 if that reports nothing; always returns 1.
evidence: Caller FieldParty_InitMemberSlots and the explicit g_actorBaseClass comparison plus the two actor update calls confirm the conditional actor update; only the caller's use is still broad.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetCursorMode
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetCursorMode(MessageWindow* self, u32 handle, int mode)
summary: Resolves an optional handle through the shared handle table (releasing the old object via virtual +0x7C), then stores the mode byte at +0x1943, where 0xFF keeps the previous mode and a stored 2 is promoted to 3.
evidence: Vtable 0x00762F48 places it in the message-window class and the +0x1942/+0x1943 state handling is read directly, but 'cursor/selection mode' is still an interpretation and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Container_HandleList_ReleaseByType
summary: Walks the handle list at self+0x10, resolves each handle through the global table and, for objects derived from g_actorBaseClass, calls virtual +0x40 with 4, then resets the list to the empty token.
evidence: The handle decode with generation check, the g_actorBaseClass walk and the vtable+0x40(4) release are clear, but the only named callee is Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyText and no caller confirms the type filter.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_AttachToOwner
summary: Resolves the tagged handle at self+0x34, walks the class chain for g_npc2DActorClassRecords and on a match calls its virtual +0x80 with (self->ownerNode, self); returns 0 when the handle is dead or of another class.
evidence: The mirror function 0x004C6D44 (detach) and the class comparison against g_npc2DActorClassRecords support the attach/detach pair, but there are no callers and the sibling itself is unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_DetachFromOwner
summary: Resolves the owner object through the handle table, checks its class tag against the 3D actor class record and invokes owner virtual slot 0xB8 with (self+0x30, self) to unregister the sprite object.
evidence: Handle lookup on self->callbackSlot, class-tag comparison against g_npc3DActorClassRecord and the virtual call 0xB8 are read directly; the owner class itself is still unnamed and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Script_FindRegisteredGlobal
summary: Lazily allocates and initialises an 8-word singleton (class tag from 0x293A00) when the cache flag is set, then hashes the VM object and walks the engine hash bucket to return the registered instance.
evidence: The one-shot init keyed by *cacheFlag and the hash-bucket walk comparing a type id are visible, but the callees (Ui_ReleaseOwnedObjects, a no-op stub) do not identify the VM, so 'script global' remains uncertain.

name: Ui_WindowPart_CreateByIndex
signature: void Ui_WindowPart_CreateByIndex(void* self, u32 index, u32 arg3)
summary: Creates or tears down one window part by index: destroys the old slot, then allocates and constructs the concrete widget class for that index (text, shop, choice, face, casino prize, message select, ...).
evidence: The only caller is the generic Ui_UpdateWindowParts, which passes a part index, and the switch then calls ~30 concrete UI constructors (Ui_BigWindow_Ctor, Ui_CasinoPrizeWindow_Ctor, Ui_MedalPrizeWindow_Ctor, Ui_CreateMessageWindow, ...); nothing in this body is talk-party specific - the talk_party.bxon literal lives in Ui_TalkParty_GetLayout - so 'Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel' was too narrow.
